text: The town started keeping a log. From now on Steampunky grows a little every other day.
Pip Wicklow built a copper-roofed pigeon coop beside the Clocktower, and the square's pigeons now roost there and circle it by day.
Ada Cogsworth and Mabel Steamwright became lunch companions, meeting on the bench in the square at noon to talk pressure gauges over sandwiches.
Tilly Fenwick moved to town and opened the Fenwick Tea Kiosk beside the Cogsworth house, pouring tea for the square and carrying pots round to the workshop and the boiler house.
Ada Cogsworth set up a brass storm glass on an iron post beside the workshop, and its needle now leaps whenever one of her experiments goes off.
Odette Quill had a roofed notice board put up on the west side of the square, where the post office pins the day's notices and lost-parcel slips.
A cast-iron hand pump was installed on the east edge of the square, and Mabel Steamwright now walks over at half past three to fetch fresh water for the boiler tank.
Captain Rook had a brass airship weathervane fixed to an iron post at the docks, and it swings round to face whichever way the wind blows.
